findings.evidence: Lines 71–72 and 139–141 expose the definitions; the only `IsMDissipative` API at lines 144–160 eliminates an existing proof and does not construct one without unfolding.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` and add characteristic iff lemmas (appropriately `[simp]`), plus an explicit constructor for `IsMDissipative`; retain the existing projection lemmas.
findings.issue: `IsDissipative` and `IsMDissipative` (line 139) are `@[expose]`, forcing consumers to unfold their representations; neither has a `*_def`/`iff` introduction API.

findings.evidence: Definition lines 139–141 quantify over every λ, while roadmap `OneParameterSemigroups/README.md` lines 145–154 specifies `∃ l₀ > 0` for `lumerPhillips`; grep finds no one-point range lemma in the PR.
findings.fix: Prove a constructor/equivalence (with the necessary completeness assumptions) deriving `IsMDissipative A` from `IsDissipative A` and `∃ λ₀ > 0, Function.Surjective (fun x : A.domain => λ₀ • (x : X) - A x)`.
findings.issue: The public `IsMDissipative` API requires surjectivity for every positive λ but provides no bridge from dissipativity plus surjectivity at one positive λ, the range condition required by the roadmap’s Lumer–Phillips interface.

summary: The dissipativity predicates expose their bodies instead of providing characteristic lemmas, and the m-dissipative API cannot consume the roadmap’s standard one-point range condition.
